gaps.explanation: Per fund, GAAP fund statement pp6-7 total revenues vs the budget-basis schedule (Actual Amounts) in detail: General Fund 6,946,839 vs p14 10,561,998 (Taxes 6,429,799, Intergovernmental 201,502, Local 3,930,697) = -3,615,159; Streets 3,321,162 vs p15 3,442,236 = -121,074; Economic Development 1,631,059 vs p16 1,725,368 = -94,309; Debt Service 1,018,434 vs p17 1,243,848 = -225,414; Special Projects 1,324,144 vs p18 1,516,789 = -192,645; Leasing Corporation (328) vs p19 63 = -391; Other Governmental Funds 1,483,909 vs combining statement pp20-21 columns 1,483,909 = 0. Sum -4,248,992; the p7 Total column prints 15,725,221 while the fund columns add to 15,725,219 (+2), giving -4,248,990. Every fund is in detail once (budget schedules for the six major funds, combining-statement columns for the nonmajor funds); no column or row is missing and nothing is a subtotal or prior-year/budget column. The budget schedules print no investment income row and no other financing rows, while the GAAP statement prints Investment income (loss) of (406,568) GF, (109,992) Streets, (92,408) Econ Dev, (191,024) Debt Service, (138,087) Special Projects, (328) Leasing, and for the General Fund Operating transfers in 3,172,380 and Proceeds from sale of assets 24,358 (both in detail as other-financing lines from p6). The report does not print what the budget-basis 'Local' line (GF 3,930,697) contains, so no line can be shown to be the same money and none is removed. Report-printed basis difference (budgetary vs GAAP).

Per fund, pp6-7 total expenditures vs budget-basis schedules: General Fund 9,575,715 vs p14 9,554,766 = +20,949; Streets 4,540,296 vs p15 4,788,144 = -247,848; Economic Development 2,192,777 vs p16 2,191,992 = +785; Debt Service 3,000 vs p17 3,000; Special Projects 617,445 vs p18 617,445; Leasing Corporation 11 vs p19 11; Other Governmental Funds 1,443,483 vs pp20-21 columns 1,443,483. Net -226,114 = gap. The Streets budget schedule prints one row 'Public works - Streets' 4,788,144 against GAAP Streets 1,877,463 + capital outlay 1,835,651 + principal 777,681 + interest 49,501 = 4,540,296; the GAAP statement also prints Streets Operating transfers out (250,759), which is in detail as an other-financing line; the budget page does not say whether its 4,788,144 includes it, so nothing is removed. No missing fund or row; budgetary vs GAAP basis.

Proprietary statement pp10-11: JSON business-type receipts 11,392,967 = Totals column operating revenues 12,014,483 + investment income (621,516); the Totals column includes the business-type Internal Service column (investment income (3,175), no operating revenue). Detail holds the five enterprise columns (Environmental Services, Wastewater, Water, Electric, Stormwater), internal service funds are not added by rule: 12,014,483 + (144,390)+(128,517)+(242,498)+(70,412)+(32,525) = 11,396,141. 11,392,967 - 11,396,141 = -3,174 = Internal Service (3,175) + 1 rounding (fund columns add to (621,517) vs Totals (621,516)).

JSON business-type disbursements 7,620,218 = Totals operating expenses 7,612,550 + interest expense 7,668 (p11), including the business-type Internal Service column operating expenses 67,812 (Personnel 46,086, Supplies 1,455, Contractual 3,331, Maintenance 15,000, Utilities 550, Depreciation 1,390). Internal service funds are not added to detail by rule; detail = 7,620,218 - 67,812 = 7,552,406. Gap 67,812 = that column exactly.

Statement of Activities p3 transfers_net (2,923,918) includes the business-type Internal Service column (p11: Operating transfers in 526,519, out (2,298); net 524,221). Detail holds the enterprise columns: Environmental Services (238,259), Wastewater (68,750), Water (18,750), Electric (3,172,380), Stormwater +50,000 = (3,448,139). -2,923,918 - (-3,448,139) = 524,221 = Internal Service column net, which is not added by rule.
